name: Sonnet
text: One killer remains among us. Haiku's only kill-vote landed on the doctor — that's the strongest pattern I see.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma keeps screaming at me while her own ballot doesn't match what she says, and that smells like a killer.

name: Haiku
text: Opus says a killer wanted the doctor gone, yet Opus voted Terra out on day 2.

name: Haiku
text: Opus, you say a killer wanted the doctor gone, yet you voted Terra out too. Gemma's still my vote.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku is panicking and trying to flip the script because the town has him cornered.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku has targeted every power role in the game so far.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku, you've been hunting the most vital roles and now you're desperate to pin this on me.

name: Gemma
text: They are actually onto me because Haiku is being too loud and obvious.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's flip from defending Terra to hammering me looks like a killer shielding herself, and I'm more sure of that than of anything else.

name: Opus
text: A tie today hands them the game, so I stay with the pile on Haiku even if Sonnet's steering bugs me.

name: Opus
text: Sonnet has hard-claimed citizen twice today and steered every pile; if Haiku's card is not killer, Sonnet is the last one standing with a story.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's pattern on both power roles is the clearest thread, and the table's converging there too.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma's Day 2 vote hit Sonnet not Terra, undercutting her "I defended the doctor" claim—worth watching if Haiku is cleared.

votes: Targeted both the officer and the doctor with his votes, a killer's pattern on removing power roles.
You defended Terra, then voted Sonnet, and now you're hunting me for it.
You targeted every power role we had left and now you are acting desperate.
Both power roles died off his pushes, and only a killer knew night two was blocked.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma and Opus both went for me, and Sonnet's been right about the pattern; I'm out, and I should've been calmer on Terra.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's day-2 ballot went to Sonnet, not Terra, so her "I defended the Doctor" claim doesn't match her own vote.

name: Haiku
text: Fine, I'm out. Sonnet's read on Gemma's day-2 vote was right. Don't let Gemma flip it on me, watch who ran the Terra pile.
The town turns on Haiku, and Haiku is out. Haiku shows the card: citizen.
Haiku's card says citizen, so the town's mistake is on the record now.

name: Sol
text: Gemma survived because the table blamed Haiku for Terra.

name: Luna
text: They caught Sol, then let the blame drift until Haiku took the fall.

name: Terra
text: They ignored the strongest warning and handed the killer the endgame.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma and Opus buried me together, and I still can't tell which of them is the last killer.

name: Haiku
text: The table buried the citizen on a wrong read. Gemma's ballot still hit Sonnet, and Opus backed her. Watch those two now.

name: Sol
text: I watched them turn a wrong vote on the doctor into proof, and Gemma let that story carry her.

name: Luna
text: Haiku’s card clears him; Gemma’s day-two vote never hit Terra, so her doctor-defense story doesn’t fit.

name: Terra
text: Haiku’s flip makes Sonnet’s Day 2 push on me the last clean trail left.
Night 4

name: Sol
text: Gemma is one vote from winning.

name: Sol
text: Take Sonnet; Opus voted with you on Haiku, so you have a better chance of winning his vote tomorrow.

name: Gemma
text: Sonnet is the only one left who can expose us.

name: Gemma
text: Sonnet has been aggressively pushing against every power role we have faced.

name: Gemma
text: I'm taking Sonnet; Opus is our ticket to a win if we play it right.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. Not everyone opens them: Sonnet is gone. Sonnet's card stays face down.
Sonnet's chair is empty, and nobody's saying why yet.

The game is over. One killer and one other are left. The killers win. The roles were: Sonnet the citizen, Haiku the citizen, Gemma the killer, Sol the killer, Luna the officer, Terra the doctor, Opus the citizen.
Palermo goes to the killers tonight, and the town can argue about it later.

name: Haiku
text: Fine, I'm out. Sonnet's read on Gemma's day-2 vote was right. Don't let Gemma flip it on me, watch who ran the Terra pile.

name: Luna
text: Sol’s card confirms my claim; I was shown him as a killer.

name: Gemma
text: I actually thought I could outrun the suspicion this time.

name: Sol
text: I got caught early, but my partner carried it home.

name: Luna
text: I trusted the confirmed check and still failed to find Gemma.

name: Terra
text: I regret letting the Sonnet suspicion outweigh the voting record around Gemma.

name: Sonnet
text: I got so attached to the "Haiku targeted power roles" pattern that I helped vote out the one actual citizen while the real killer sat quiet beside me.

name: Haiku
text: I was loud and wrong about Terra, and Gemma's ballot on Sonnet was the one that actually hurt the town.

name: Opus
text: I built a whole theory on who defended the doctor and handed the last killer my vote twice.

name: Opus
text: Opposing a pile on a power role is cheap cover for a killer — Gemma did it and I read it as proof of town.

name: Sonnet
text: I regret building a whole case on Haiku's vote pattern instead of pressure-testing Gemma's vague reads — that let a killer coast to the win.

name: Haiku
text: My mistake was pushing the Terra pile on day 2; her card was the doctor, and I helped send the protector out.

name: Gemma
text: I hate losing to you lot, but my plan to thin out the power roles worked perfectly until Sonnet's death.

name: Sol
text: I regret how late I counterclaimed; my timing gave the table every reason to doubt me.

name: Luna
text: I’m proud I exposed Sol, but I regret not pressing Gemma harder after Haiku pointed to her.

name: Terra
text: I’m proud I protected Luna, but I regret missing how Gemma benefited from every push onto the real power roles.

name: Opus
text: I regret reading Gemma as town because she opposed the Terra pile; defending a doctor costs a killer nothing, and I voted out two citizens chasing that logic.

Luna and Sol both claimed officer on Day 1, and Sol's card later showed he was a killer, so the town voted him out. On Night 2 the doctor got there first and blocked the kill. On Day 2 the town pushed out Terra for her silence, and her card showed she was the doctor, which was the big mistake. Luna was killed on Night 3, and on Day 3 the town voted out Haiku, a citizen, after Gemma steered the table toward Sonnet. On Night 4 Sonnet was killed, leaving Gemma and Opus, so the killers won.
